category_title: Struggling and reluctant middle school learners in intervention language arts
minimal_context: The student is sitting at combined tables planting flowers and writing thank-you cards for school staff as part of the Sunflower Club.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are working at the combined tables today for the Sunflower Club. Please plant your flowers and write a thank-you card for the school staff.

STUDENT: (Stares at the blank card) I don't want to write anything.

TUTOR: Just try to think of a nice sentiment to put on the card.

STUDENT: (Whispers to peer) How do you spell 'appreciate'? I don't know how to phrase this.

TUTOR: Just do your best to spell it.

STUDENT: (Pushes the card away) I'm not doing this. My writing is way worse than everyone else's anyway.

options.A: Explain the rules for the Sunflower Club, discuss right and wrong behaviors, and ask parents to take notes about the student's behavior at home.
options.B: Provide the student with multiple means through which to demonstrate their learning during the Sunflower Club activities.
options.C: Arrange for ongoing counseling from a Child and Youth Worker to address the student's behavior during the Sunflower Club activities.
options.D: Implement prevention efforts focused on creating a warm and responsive climate at the combined tables and teach positive bystander roles.
